projects.name: Awantika Residence
projects.idea: One material decides the house. Everything else steps back.
projects.brief: Awantika Residence is a villa in Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, designed by Form X's architects around two stones. Green stone wraps the living room's TV wall around a single white marble slab, and the sofas pick up the same green in velvet. Black marble takes over in the open kitchen, where the island doubles as a breakfast bar, then returns as the backlit shelving of the study nook and home office. Two materials, used wherever they appear, keep eight different views reading as one house.

projects.name: Suba Residence
projects.idea: Double height can feel like a lobby. Curves and warm stone make it a home.
projects.brief: Suba Residence is a villa in Hyderabad where the living room rises a full two floors. Form X's architects kept that height from feeling like a lobby: a curved velvet sofa, a travertine wall and a gold-leaf chandelier sized for the void bring it down to human scale. The kitchen pairs a marble backsplash with an island and green velvet bar stools, while a galley kitchen with built-in ovens handles the heavy cooking. Meals move between a dining room under a leaf chandelier and a walnut-panelled nook with sculptural chairs.

projects.name: Jagadeesh Residence
projects.idea: Height is a material. Use it, or stop paying for it.
projects.brief: Jagadeesh Residence is a villa in Narsingi, Hyderabad, planned by Form X's architects around its height. The double-height living room carries a chandelier and a TV wall scaled to both floors, and an indoor courtyard with a tree pulls daylight into the middle of the house. A Buddha console under a fluted ceiling marks the foyer; the family lounge has diamond-pattern timber panelling and a low sofa on a timber plinth. The bedrooms pair beds with built-in study and dressing units, and a walk-in wardrobe has its own dressing table.

projects.name: Sathish Residence
projects.idea: Choose one geometry and carry it through. Here, it is the angle.
projects.brief: Sathish Residence is a villa in Hyderabad where Form X's architects let one geometry run the house: the angle. It starts in the kitchen with a faceted island, oak tall units and an angled chimney, and continues as chevron timber panelling in the foyer lounge and beside the marble TV wall. A home office with a glass bookcase sits on a raised platform, and the study is set a few steps up behind a glass partition. On the first floor, a lounge opens to floor-to-ceiling windows.

projects.name: Pranithi Residence
projects.idea: The joinery is the architecture. Shape the room with built-ins, not with furniture.
projects.brief: Pranithi Residence is an apartment in Narsingi, Hyderabad, where Form X's architects let the built-ins shape every room. The living room is organised by a media wall with a lit glass display tower and vertical slats, a fluted-glass partition shelf separates the dining area, and a teak-and-glass pooja room sits beside the TV wall. In the bedrooms, sliding wardrobes, lofts, study desks and a window seat are planned into the walls, so the floor stays free. The taupe L-shaped kitchen adds tall pantry units around the fridge.

projects.idea: Repeat one shape and the whole home holds together. Here, it is the arch.
projects.brief: Saranya Residence is a 3BHK apartment in Hyderabad, designed by Form X's architects with one shape and one palette. Arched mirrors appear twice, over the living room console and at the dining wash basin, and a dome pendant hangs above the marble dining table. The living room pairs a grey sectional with blue art and a TV unit on a floating console. The bedrooms work in greys and charcoal, with a fluted headboard wall and a wardrobe-and-study unit in the master. The kitchen has fluted-glass cabinets, a sink at the window, built-in ovens and a utility door.

projects.idea: One matte taupe, kitchen shutters to wardrobes. That is what keeps a full home calm.

projects.name: Zen Co-Work
projects.idea: Let colour do the zoning. Terracotta to work, blush to meet, the mural to switch off.
projects.brief: Zen Co-Work is a coworking office in Hyderabad where Form X's architects used colour to zone the floor. A terracotta sofa and a hot-desk counter sit beside a geometric mural in the lounge, and black-framed glass cabins line the open workstations. Desks in the workstation bays pick up the terracotta, panelled walls carry the storage, and the meeting room turns blush pink, so every zone reads at a glance.
projects.title: Startup Office Interior Design, Hyderabad | Zen · Form X
projects.meta: A geometric mural, terracotta desks and glass cabins: see how Form X's architects zoned Zen Co-Work, a startup office in Hyderabad, with colour.
